skill.description: Build stronger TypeScript systems with advanced types, generics, strict compiler settings, decorators, and enterprise architecture patterns.
skill.summary: Guides advanced TypeScript architecture, strict type safety, and maintainable type design.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: Static analysis reported no suspicious patterns in the single prompt-only skill file. Manual review of SKILL.md found TypeScript guidance only, with no prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, or executable code.

content.user_title: Improve TypeScript Architecture and Type Safety
content.value_statement: Complex TypeScript projects can lose safety when types, configs, and contracts grow unevenly. This skill guides strict typing, advanced type design, and maintainable architecture.
actual_capabilities: Designs TypeScript architectures and shared type contracts.
Explains generics, conditional types, mapped types, and utility types.
Recommends strict compiler settings and TSConfig improvements.
Reviews type inference choices for clarity and maintainability.
Guides decorators, metadata patterns, modules, and namespace organization.
Suggests typed tests, declaration files, and TSDoc coverage.
limitations: Does not execute compiler checks without project access.
Requires project context, runtime targets, and strictness goals.
Cannot replace local test, lint, and build validation.

use_cases.title: Harden Shared Types
use_cases.description: Review shared models, API contracts, and utility types before they spread across a codebase.

use_cases.title: Plan Strict Migration
use_cases.description: Move a growing project toward strict TypeScript with staged compiler and linting safeguards.

use_cases.title: Resolve Type Complexity
use_cases.description: Untangle advanced generics, inference failures, and type performance issues in framework code.

prompt_templates.title: Review Type Safety
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a small TypeScript area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript file for type safety issues. Explain the main risks and suggest simpler, safer types.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Shared Contracts
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate design of shared interfaces and utility types.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me redesign these shared TypeScript contracts. Focus on generics, constraints, readability, and backward compatibility.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Strict Configuration
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced migration toward strict compiler settings.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a staged plan to improve our TSConfig strictness. Include likely errors, migration order, and build performance checks.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Enterprise Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced architecture review for a large TypeScript system.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this TypeScript architecture for module boundaries, advanced type design, decorators, tests, and declaration file strategy.

output_examples.input: A service layer uses broad object types and weak API response contracts.
output_examples.output: The skill identifies unsafe boundaries, proposes named contracts, and recommends validation points with clearer generic constraints.

output_examples.input: A team wants to enable stricter compiler settings without blocking delivery.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a staged migration plan with priority flags, likely failure areas, and build performance checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A library exposes confusing utility types that slow development.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests simpler type names, safer constraints, inference improvements, and documentation targets for maintainers.

best_practices: Share runtime targets, TypeScript version, and current TSConfig before asking for architecture guidance.
Ask for tradeoffs between strictness, readability, and build performance when changing shared types.
Validate recommendations with local compiler, lint, and test runs before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not request advanced type tricks when simple interfaces would be clearer.
Do not enable strict settings without a staged migration plan.
Do not rely on generated type advice without checking runtime behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill write production TypeScript?
faq.answer: It can guide TypeScript design and implementation, but local testing and review remain required.

faq.question: Can it help with strict mode migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan staged TSConfig changes and explain likely compiler issues.

faq.question: Does it support React and Node.js projects?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill mentions React, Node.js, and Express integration patterns.

faq.question: Can it optimize type inference?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review inference issues and suggest clearer generic constraints.

faq.question: Does it run TypeScript builds?
faq.answer: No. It is a prompt-only skill and does not execute builds by itself.

faq.question: Is it suitable for JavaScript-only projects?
faq.answer: No. The skill is intended for projects that use or plan to enforce TypeScript.
